# dla_syamv

> Computes a matrix-vector product `y := alpha*|A|*|x| + beta*|y|` using a symmetric indefinite matrix to calculate error bounds.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dlaSyamv from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dla_syamv';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dla_syamv( order, uplo, N, alpha, A, LDA, x, strideX, beta, y, strideY ) → Float64Array
```

Computes `y := alpha*|A|*|x| + beta*|y|` using a symmetric indefinite matrix to calculate error bounds.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | Storage layout (`'row-major'` or `'column-major'`) |
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | Specifies whether the upper or lower triangular part of `A` is referenced (`'upper'` or `'lower'`) |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of the matrix `A`<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `alpha` | `number` | Scalar constant |
| `A` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | Input matrix |
| ↳ `LDA` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `A`<br>Requires `LDA ≥ max(1, N)` |
| `x` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | Input vector |
| ↳ `strideX` | `integer` | Stride length for `x` |
| `beta` | `number` | Scalar constant |
| `y` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **in/out** · Input/output vector |
| ↳ `strideY` | `integer` | Stride length for `y` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `uplo`: On entry, `UPLO` specifies whether the upper or lower triangular part of the array A is to be referenced as follows:

  `UPLO = BLAS_UPPER` Only the upper triangular part of A

  is to be referenced.

  `UPLO = BLAS_LOWER` Only the lower triangular part of A

  is to be referenced.

  Unchanged on exit.
- `N`: On entry, N specifies the number of columns of the matrix A. N must be at least zero. Unchanged on exit.
- `alpha`: On entry, `ALPHA` specifies the scalar $\alpha$. Unchanged on exit.
- `A`: Before entry, the leading m by n part of the array A must contain the matrix of coefficients. Unchanged on exit.
- `x`: Before entry, the incremented array X must contain the vector x. Unchanged on exit.
- `beta`: On entry, `BETA` specifies the scalar $\beta$. When `BETA` is supplied as zero then Y need not be set on input. Unchanged on exit.
- `y`: Before entry with `BETA` non-zero, the incremented array Y must contain the vector y. On exit, Y is overwritten by the updated vector y.

</details>

**Returns** `Float64Array`: `y`

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `TypeError` second argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `RangeError` third argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` sixth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )`
- `RangeError` eighth argument must be non-zero
- `RangeError` eleventh argument must be non-zero

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dla_syamv.ndarray(
    uplo,
    N,
    alpha,
    A, strideA1, strideA2, offsetA,
    x, strideX, offsetX,
    beta,
    y, strideY, offsetY
) → Float64Array
```

Computes `y := alpha*|A|*|x| + beta*|y|` using a symmetric indefinite matrix to calculate error bounds.

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | Specifies whether the upper or lower triangular part of `A` is referenced (`'upper'` or `'lower'`) |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of the matrix `A`<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `alpha` | `number` | Scalar constant |
| `A` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | Input matrix |
| ↳ `strideA1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `A` |
| ↳ `strideA2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `A` |
| ↳ `offsetA` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `A` |
| `x` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | Input vector |
| ↳ `strideX` | `integer` | Stride length for `x` |
| ↳ `offsetX` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `x` |
| `beta` | `number` | Scalar constant |
| `y` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **in/out** · Input/output vector |
| ↳ `strideY` | `integer` | Stride length for `y` |
| ↳ `offsetY` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `y` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `uplo`: On entry, `UPLO` specifies whether the upper or lower triangular part of the array A is to be referenced as follows:

  `UPLO = BLAS_UPPER` Only the upper triangular part of A

  is to be referenced.

  `UPLO = BLAS_LOWER` Only the lower triangular part of A

  is to be referenced.

  Unchanged on exit.
- `N`: On entry, N specifies the number of columns of the matrix A. N must be at least zero. Unchanged on exit.
- `alpha`: On entry, `ALPHA` specifies the scalar $\alpha$. Unchanged on exit.
- `A`: Before entry, the leading m by n part of the array A must contain the matrix of coefficients. Unchanged on exit.
- `x`: Before entry, the incremented array X must contain the vector x. Unchanged on exit.
- `beta`: On entry, `BETA` specifies the scalar $\beta$. When `BETA` is supplied as zero then Y need not be set on input. Unchanged on exit.
- `y`: Before entry with `BETA` non-zero, the incremented array Y must contain the vector y. On exit, Y is overwritten by the updated vector y.

</details>

**Returns** `Float64Array`: `y`

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `RangeError` second argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` ninth argument must be non-zero
- `RangeError` thirteenth argument must be non-zero

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `dla_syamv()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`DLA_SYAMV`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/dla_syamv.f).
-   Computes `y := alpha*|A|*|x| + beta*|y|` using the symmetric matrix `A`; both triangles of `A` contribute via symmetry regardless of which triangle is referenced.
-   To protect against underflow, non-symbolically-zero components are perturbed by `(N+1)` times the underflow threshold. An entry is considered "symbolically zero" only when every multiplication contributing to it has a zero operand.
-   This routine is primarily used in LAPACK error-bound computations (e.g., `dsyrfsx`).

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
/* eslint-disable camelcase, stdlib/require-file-extensions */

import discreteUniform from '@stdlib/random/array/discrete-uniform/lib/index.js';
import dla_syamv from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dla_syamv';

/** @type {{ dtype: 'float64' }} */
const opts = {
	'dtype': 'float64'
};

const N = 3;
const A = discreteUniform( N * N, -10, 10, opts );
const x = discreteUniform( N, -10, 10, opts );
const y = discreteUniform( N, -10, 10, opts );

dla_syamv( 'row-major', 'upper', N, 1.0, A, N, x, 1, 0.0, y, 1 );
console.log( y ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DLA_SYAMV`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DLA\_SYAMV performs the matrix-vector operation

$$
y := \alpha \, \lvert A \rvert \, \lvert x \rvert + \beta \, \lvert y \rvert
$$

where $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are scalars, x and y are vectors and A is an n by n symmetric matrix.

This function is primarily used in calculating error bounds. To protect against underflow during evaluation, components in the resulting vector are perturbed away from zero by (N+1) times the underflow threshold. To prevent unnecessarily large errors for block-structure embedded in general matrices, "symbolically" zero components are not perturbed. A zero entry is considered "symbolic" if all multiplications involved in computing that entry have at least one zero multiplicand.

### Further Details

Level 2 Blas routine.

</section>
